statement: Let n = len(dist), s = speed, H = hoursBefore. For a subset S of {0,1,...,n-2}, let A(S) be the arrival time when exactly the rests indexed by S are skipped, defined as follows. Set tau = 0. For i = 0,1,...,n-1: set tau := tau + dist[i]/s, where division is exact real division; if i < n-1 and i is not in S, set tau := ceil(tau), where ceil(x) is the least integer >= x; if i < n-1 and i is in S, leave tau unchanged. After processing i = n-1, A(S) is the final value of tau. The function returns a result r, and: if there exists S subset of {0,1,...,n-2} with A(S) <= H, then r = min { |S| : S subset of {0,1,...,n-2} and A(S) <= H }; otherwise r = -1.
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: When the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 0 <= r <= n-1, where n = len(dist).
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: When the function returns a result r, r = -1 if and only if sum_{i=0}^{n-1} dist[i] > hoursBefore * speed, where n = len(dist).
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: Let n = len(dist), s = speed, H = hoursBefore, and let A(empty) be the arrival time when no rests are skipped, computed by the recurrence in the main specification with S = empty. When the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if A(empty) <= H.
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: Let n = len(dist), s = speed, H = hoursBefore, and define A(S) as in the main specification. When the function returns a result r and r >= 0, there exists a subset S of {0,1,...,n-2} such that |S| = r and A(S) <= H.
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: Let n = len(dist), s = speed, H = hoursBefore, and define A(S) as in the main specification. When the function returns a result r and r >= 0, for every subset S of {0,1,...,n-2} with |S| < r, we have A(S) > H.
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: If n = len(dist) = 1, then when the function returns a result r, r = 0 if dist[0] <= hoursBefore * speed, and r = -1 if dist[0] > hoursBefore * speed.
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: Let n = len(dist), s = speed, H = hoursBefore, define A(S) as in the main specification, and let S_all = {0,1,...,n-2}. When the function returns a result r, r = n-1 if and only if A(S_all) <= H and for every subset S of {0,1,...,n-2} with |S| < n-1, A(S) > H.
preconditions: n = len(dist); 1 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000; 1 <= speed <= 1000000; 1 <= hoursBefore <= 10000000. All integers are 64-bit signed integers within the stated ranges.

statement: Let r(H) denote the result of min_skips(dist, speed, H) for H in [1, 10000000]. When both calls min_skips(dist, speed, H1) and min_skips(dist, speed, H2) return results r1 and r2, either r1 = -1, or (r2 != -1 and r2 <= r1).
preconditions: dist is a slice of n Int64 values with n = len(dist), 1 <= n <= 1000, and 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n; speed is an integer with 1 <= speed <= 1000000; H1 and H2 are integers with 1 <= H1 <= H2 <= 10000000.

statement: Let r(s) denote the result of min_skips(dist, s, H) for s in [1, 1000000]. When both calls min_skips(dist, s1, H) and min_skips(dist, s2, H) return results r1 and r2, either r1 = -1, or (r2 != -1 and r2 <= r1).
preconditions: dist is a slice of n Int64 values with n = len(dist), 1 <= n <= 1000, and 1 <= dist[i] <= 100000 for every 0 <= i < n; H is an integer with 1 <= H <= 10000000; s1 and s2 are integers with 1 <= s1 <= s2 <= 1000000.
